Discover the terroir, meticulous processing, and the spirit of Chinese tea culture within these exceptional leaves.

programme.title: Dreams beyond the acrobatic stage
programme.desc: Many young acrobats from across China have gathered in Wuqiao, Cangzhou in north China's Hebei Province, with one shared goal: to dazzle audiences with their talents and stunt skills. They usually starts to train at an early age, shouldering the hopes and support of their families and teachers to become successful performers. We followed three of these young performers to show you how incredibly talented they are.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-4 Medieval Combat
programme.desc: Episode 4 centres on Shanghai, where Eastern and Western martial traditions meet in surprising ways. Kleber visits local practitioners of Historical European Martial Arts (HEMA), trying German and Italian longsword techniques first-hand and seeing how Chinese enthusiasts innovate by combining European swordsmanship with ancient Chinese military manuals. The episode also follows the rise of BUHURT, a European-style armored combat sport now gaining traction in China, featuring locally made traditional Chinese armour in intense full-contact bouts. Through Kleber’s own multicultural martial arts studio and the city’s everyday East-West blend, the episode shows Shanghai as a global hub, a place where classical martial arts find new life and cross-cultural practices thrive.

programme.title: Foodwise: The Taste of Home
programme.desc: In this episode, our hosts Tianran He and Eva May eat their way down memory lane across virtual space and different time zones, and embark on a culinary journey at their birthplace. Eva rediscovers her love for a classic century-old dish in her hometown Vienna and introduces Austria's long-lasting coffeehouse culture to Tianran, who also joins her virtually for an evening with friends and food the traditional Viennese way. Meanwhile, Beijing's charming autumn season sets Tianran back in time as he rediscovers flavors from his childhood. His passion for tea might have even started in one of the old tea shops in Beijing's hutongs, recollecting his memories one sip at a time, accompanied by nostalgic meals and a relaxed stroll under yellow gingko trees.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoxing
programme.desc: Join host Tianran He in the historic water town of Shaoxing, famed for its yellow wine. Traversing its canals by boat, Tianran discovers why it's said there are 10,000 bridges in Shaoxing, before enjoying the freshest catch of the day. But as it turns out, Shaoxing's climate is also perfect for fermentation, leading to a wide array of unique local foods that can sometimes be both smelly and delicious – and at other times, downright unforgettable!

programme.title: Celebrating the Corban Festival
programme.desc: Kashgar, situated in the southwest of Xinjiang, was a key stop on the ancient Silk Road. It served as a gateway for trade between China and countries in Asia and Europe. However, it wasn’t only goods that were exchanged on the Silk Road. So, too, were cultures, which merged and flourished. In the 7th century AD, Islam entered China’s western regions along the Silk Road, bringing with it the Corban Festival. With time, Corban became more than a religious festival. It developed into a traditional holiday celebrated by everyone in Kashgar. Corban is as important as New Year. Kashgar locals load their tables with food on this day to reward themselves for a year of hard work. Corban is all about sharing. In the past, rich families would buy extra meat to share with their neighbors and friends. This tradition is still alive in Kashgar today, although it’s practiced not just by the rich, but pretty well everyone.

programme.title: China Highly Recommended: Changsha
programme.desc: Episode 1 of Travelogue's "China Highly Recommended" tells the story of Changsha, one of China's happiest cities. Following the lives of four of its foreign residents: A French executive chef, a Japanese podcaster, and two American teachers, we discover the reasons why they made Changsha their second home, and explore the city with them as only locals do. This episode will be released as a 30 minute travel documentary to be broadcast on CGTN's television channel and social media platform, along with a series of video clips and photos

programme.title: China Untapped: Nanjing 3
programme.desc: Join us in Nanjing’s bustling old quarter, where you can try on silk dresses worth their weight in gold, and see how traditional handicrafts have been given modern twists. We’ll feast on street snacks and local delicacies by the old Confucian Temple, before taking a pleasure cruise along Nanjing’s mother river to round off our exploration of this vibrant and historic city.

programme.title: Valentine's with the Snake King
programme.desc: Every year on Qixi Festival (Chinese Valentine's Day), the town of Zhanghu in Nanping, Fujian Province hosts a folk custom event: the Snake King Parade. Local residents carry the statue of the Snake King from the temple, along with specially prepared pythons, and parade through the streets and alleys. Wherever the procession passes, residents and shopkeepers greet them with firecrackers and burn incense to pray, hoping to receive the unique blessing of the Snake King. This distinctive folk activity is rarely seen elsewhere across China. Taking this event as its highlight, the episode leads audiences on a deep dive into the towns and villages of northern Fujian, delivering a highly engaging and visually appealing viewing experience.

programme.title: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River
programme.desc: Ningxia: Echoes of the Yellow River is a documentary focusing on the World Heritage sites and cultural–ecological conservation in the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region. Through the lens of Ningxia’s heritage stories, the film highlights China’s commitment to World Heritage preservation, ecological restoration, and cultural continuity — presenting to global audiences a land where history and modernity intertwine, and where desert and oasis coexist. By following the guardians of the Western Xia Imperial Tombs, desert restorers in the Tengger Desert, Great Wall rangers at Sanguankou, traditional sheepskin raft craftsmen, and managers of the Yellow River irrigation system in Qingtongxia, the program reveals Ningxia’s distinctive contributions to cultural heritage, natural ecology, and intangible traditions — and the enduring human spirit behind them.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-5 Xingyi Quan
programme.desc: In Episode 5, Kleber travels to Shanxi, the birthplace of Xingyi Quan. He follows Master Cao Bing, a traditional Xingyi Quan teacher and modern combat coach, from Taiyuan’s noodle shops to Pingyao’s ancient streets, and from centuries-old vinegar breweries to Guandi temples, exploring Xingyi Quan’s deep links to Shanxi’s merchant culture and history. Master Cao breaks down the core principles of the “Five Elements and Twelve Forms”, and shows in his modern gym how techniques found in Muay Thai and Jiu-Jitsu can be integrated without losing Xingyi Quan’s philosophical core, guided by the mindset of taking only what is essential. Set against ancient sites such as Yongle Palace, this episode shows how true inner strength is like traditional timber architecture: stable, balanced, and built from within.

programme.title: Foodwise: Haikou
programme.desc: Welcome to Haikou, also known as the Coconut City! Join Tianran He in experiencing the unique culinary culture and urban character of this tropical paradise. From light and sweet coconut chicken hotpot to refreshing herbal desserts and spicy rice soup - a local favourite, every bite tells the story of the city's laid-back charm and beauty. We'll explore everything from Haikou's winding alleys and mangrove forests, to the culture of its southeast Asian diaspora, so come and discover this magical destination with us.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programme.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan’s four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programme.title: Four Faces of Muqam
programme.desc: Muqam is a performing art with its roots in the folklore of Xinjiang. Rather like an encyclopedia, Muqam is a record of the history and lifestyle of the local Uygur people. It originated in folk culture, with lyrics that covered everything from philosophical aphorisms to folk tales. Muqam is a vehicle for Uygur people to express their feelings and ideas. As such, it is an integral part of Xinjiang culture—and even the culture of the Silk Road. In the episode, the host travels around the Kashgar area, learning about the history and art of Muqam.

programme.title: Kung fu journey up Wudang Mountains
programme.desc: Located in central China's Hubei Province, Wudang Mountains is a UNESCO World Natural and Cultural Heritage site recognized as the cradle of Wudang kung fu and as a renowned Taoist sanctuary. Every year, young students from different parts of China flock to these well-established kung fu academies to experience a childhood like no other. Li Weimu and Li Muzi study at two separate kung fu academies, and are following their own paths at Wudang Mountains.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Mount Siguniang
programme.desc: In this episode, Host Tianran He is on a mission: To reach the summit of Mount Siguniang, a towering snowcapped mountain in southwestern China. Together with his friend Ma Chunlin, a photographer for National Geographic, they trek through one of China’s most beautiful and biodiverse hiking routes, before making for base camp. But with worsening weather conditions and severe altitude sickness, the odds are stacked against them. Ten years ago, Tianran failed his attempt at climbing Mount Siguniang’s First Peak – this time, he’s all in.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.1
programme.desc: Join Tianran He in Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. Fed by the Yarlung Zangbo River and abundant rainfall, this lush subtropical region is home to some of Xizan’g most unique scenery. From sacred mountains and ancient monasteries, to cruising along Nyingchi’s mother river, wandering alpine meadows and savoring stone pot chicken – a beloved local delicacy, Tianran uncovers the beauty of Nyingchi.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: “The Pulse” features musicians performing amidst Guizhou’s stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: Jingmai Wanderings: A Symphony of Humans and Tea
programme.desc: As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Mount Jingmai embodies the ecological wisdom of forest–tea symbiosis and the rich cultural diversity of its ethnic communities. It plays a vital role in biodiversity conservation and the preservation of traditional tea culture. This episode follows the stories of representative individuals to explore three key themes — heritage preservation, ecological sustainability, and youth empowerment — revealing the unique charm and sustainable development model of Mount Jingmai.

programme.title: Kung Fu Wise II-5 Xingyi Quan
programme.desc: In Episode 5, Kleber travels to Shanxi, the birthplace of Xingyi Quan. He follows Master Cao Bing, a traditional Xingyi Quan teacher and modern combat coach, from Taiyuan’s noodle shops to Pingyao’s ancient streets, and from centuries-old vinegar breweries to Guandi temples, exploring Xingyi Quan’s deep links to Shanxi’s merchant culture and history. Master Cao breaks down the core principles of the “Five Elements and Twelve Forms”, and shows in his modern gym how techniques found in Muay Thai and Jiu-Jitsu can be integrated without losing Xingyi Quan’s philosophical core, guided by the mindset of taking only what is essential. Set against ancient sites such as Yongle Palace, this episode shows how true inner strength is like traditional timber architecture: stable, balanced, and built from within.

programme.title: Foodwise: Haikou
programme.desc: Welcome to Haikou, also known as the Coconut City! Join Tianran He in experiencing the unique culinary culture and urban character of this tropical paradise. From light and sweet coconut chicken hotpot to refreshing herbal desserts and spicy rice soup - a local favourite, every bite tells the story of the city's laid-back charm and beauty. We'll explore everything from Haikou's winding alleys and mangrove forests, to the culture of its southeast Asian diaspora, so come and discover this magical destination with us.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hainan's Four Famous Dishes
programme.desc: The stunning east coast of Hainan in southeast China, attract numerous visitors to travel. The reason that people tend to visit Hianan not only because of the beautiful beach view but also delicious local cuisine in Hainan. Hainan’s four famous dishes is Chicken, duck, goat and crab. In Wenchang, the ancestral home of many overseas Chinese, people could discover the original version of Hainan Chicken Rice and see how local chickens free range on coconut meat. In Qionghai, seat of the Boao Forum for Asia, you may dine on duck and goat, before feasting on crab in the surfer haven of Wanning.

programme.title: Four Faces of Muqam
programme.desc: Muqam is a performing art with its roots in the folklore of Xinjiang. Rather like an encyclopedia, Muqam is a record of the history and lifestyle of the local Uygur people. It originated in folk culture, with lyrics that covered everything from philosophical aphorisms to folk tales. Muqam is a vehicle for Uygur people to express their feelings and ideas. As such, it is an integral part of Xinjiang culture—and even the culture of the Silk Road. In the episode, the host travels around the Kashgar area, learning about the history and art of Muqam.

programme.title: Kung fu journey up Wudang Mountains
programme.desc: Located in central China's Hubei Province, Wudang Mountains is a UNESCO World Natural and Cultural Heritage site recognized as the cradle of Wudang kung fu and as a renowned Taoist sanctuary. Every year, young students from different parts of China flock to these well-established kung fu academies to experience a childhood like no other. Li Weimu and Li Muzi study at two separate kung fu academies, and are following their own paths at Wudang Mountains.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Mount Siguniang
programme.desc: In this episode, Host Tianran He is on a mission: To reach the summit of Mount Siguniang, a towering snowcapped mountain in southwestern China. Together with his friend Ma Chunlin, a photographer for National Geographic, they trek through one of China’s most beautiful and biodiverse hiking routes, before making for base camp. But with worsening weather conditions and severe altitude sickness, the odds are stacked against them. Ten years ago, Tianran failed his attempt at climbing Mount Siguniang’s First Peak – this time, he’s all in.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.1
programme.desc: Join Tianran He in Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. Fed by the Yarlung Zangbo River and abundant rainfall, this lush subtropical region is home to some of Xizan’g most unique scenery. From sacred mountains and ancient monasteries, to cruising along Nyingchi’s mother river, wandering alpine meadows and savoring stone pot chicken – a beloved local delicacy, Tianran uncovers the beauty of Nyingchi.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: “The Pulse” features musicians performing amidst Guizhou’s stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: Jingmai Wanderings: A Symphony of Humans and Tea
programme.desc: As a UNESCO World Heritage site, Mount Jingmai embodies the ecological wisdom of forest–tea symbiosis and the rich cultural diversity of its ethnic communities. It plays a vital role in biodiversity conservation and the preservation of traditional tea culture. This episode follows the stories of representative individuals to explore three key themes — heritage preservation, ecological sustainability, and youth empowerment — revealing the unique charm and sustainable development model of Mount Jingmai.

programme.title: Pingyao Hand-Polished Lacquer Art
programme.desc: Pingyao is an old town with a history of over 2,700 years in the north of China, in Shanxi Province. The rich cultural heritage it built up over the centuries eventually gave rise to a very special art—Tuiguang lacquerware. This hand-polished lacquerware, unique to Pingyao, is recognized as one of the four representative lacquerwares of China.

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.1
programme.desc: What's not to love about Xishuangbanna? From dazzling night markets to lush bamboo forests, 800-year old tea trees to close encounters with elephants, this tropical city in southwest China has everything, and is where the story of tea begins. Join Foodwise for all the Pu'er tea you can drink and feast on everything from banana flowers to "elephant food"!

programme.title: Foodwise: Xishuangbanna Ep.2
programme.desc: Come get soaked at the Dai people's New Year celebrations! We'll check out buzzing street markets packed with barbecued meats and spicy fruits, crash a foodie auction, and even take part in a rowdy competition, catching fish with our bare hands in the river. All this before hiking through an actual rainforest. We're going to need all the good tea and food we can get!

programme.title: The Sichuan Zhuqin
programme.desc: Sichuan Zhuqin is a national intangible cultural heritage in China. Nowadays, its performances are constantly innovated, with new styles such as ensemble emerging. Creators have broken traditional performance methods, integrating Zhuqin with traditional Chinese instruments like the guzheng and erhu, and also experimenting with contemporary music forms such as rap and folk rock, aiming to make this traditional art appeal to more young audiences.

programme.title: Breathing new life into century-old Yueju Opera
programme.desc: Yueju Opera is one of the five major Chinese operas. It is skillful in narration and sentiment and is popular across China. This timeless form of intangible cultural heritage now has new apprentices. We followed a young duo of Yueju Opera performers: eleven-year-old Wang Yuhan and her stage partner, nine-year-old Huang Xinru in Ningbo, Zhejiang Province, as they shared kindred spirits in inheriting the performing art of Yueju Opera.

programme.title: Thrill Seeker’s Guide to China: Changbai Mountain
programme.desc: An unforgettable adventure awaits amidst the breathtaking landscapes of Changbai Mountain! Embark on a trek through pristine birch forests, marvel at the majestic power of the world's deepest volcanic waterfall, and uncover hidden gems along the way. Indulge in soaking in natural hot springs and experience exhilarating rafting down mountain streams, all leading to the final destination: Tianchi Lake, a heavenly oasis nestled in the clouds. Join the Travelogue team as we delve into the beauty of Changbai Mountain.

programme.title: Nyingchi Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He continues his journey through Nyingchi, Xizang Autonomous Region. He meets the Lhoba people, China’s smallest ethnic group, who show him their traditional hunting attire. At a sacred lake, Tianran visits an ancient monastery and witnesses the 3000-year-old dance of the Gongbo Tibetans, before venturing to a remote village to experience their their way of life.

programme.title: The Pulse

programme.title: Back to the Land: Exploring new life in rural China
programme.desc: When we think of the countryside, what colour comes to mind? The answer lies in Wuxin—Wood, Fire, Earth, Metal and Water—an ancient rhythm that still pulses beneath China’s landscapes. In this programme, we explore how the colours of Wuxing come to life through the traditions of China’s ethnic minority groups. From Lugu Lake’s matrilineal water world and the metal-hued fire of the Yi Torch Festival, to Dali’s earth-driven crafts, Guizhou’s wooden Dong dwellings, and the volcanic winds of Inner Mongolia’s new nomadic life—the Five Elements guide the stories of people reconnecting with land, culture and community.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Wing Chun
programme.desc: Martial arts lover Kleber Battaglia is on a mission: To seek out China's kungfu masters, and learn their secrets. From explosive Wing Chun to fluid Taiji Quan, slippery Snake Style to elegant White Crane, he'll learn hidden moves and ancient techniques for defeating powerful opponents. But ?there’s more to kungfu than combat: From culture and philosophy, to wellness and insights from the natural world, Kleber will discover that contained within every kick, strike and throw, is the condensed wisdom of the ancient masters. This is Kungfu-wise. Kleber travels to Foshan, the birthplace of Wing Chun. A practitioner of this style, he seeks out masters of two different lineages: Ip Man and Snake Style. First he visits the Ip Man lineage, based on the legendary kungfu master whose life story spawned hundreds of martial arts movies, with Bruce Lee counting among his students. With Ip Man Wing Chun, Kleber learns how to create powerful short strikes perfectly suited to fighting in Foshan’s narrow alleys. With Snake Style, he experiences unique training methods that give its practitioners superhuman flexibility, allowing them to stick to their opponents, and even fight on boats in canals

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.1
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah climb Mount.Huangshan, one of China's most famous mountains, sampling its delicate green tea and the rich flavors of Anhui cuisine, and explore the region's ancient villages and lush bamboo forests featured in the blockbuster film "Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon".

programme.title: Foodwise: Huangshan Ep.2
programme.desc: In Huangshan, Anhui Province, the hosts enjoy a cup of Queen Elizabeth II's favorite tea, as well as the oldest green tea to be exported Europe, and get hands on with quirky local delicacies ranging from "word candy" and tofu made of leaves, to the downright funky flavors of hairy tofu and stinky mandarin fish.

programme.title: The Tongliang Dragon Dance
programme.desc: The Tongliang Dragon Dance is a traditional performance art rooted in Chongqing’s Tongliang District, characterized by its elaborate dragon props and dynamic choreography. Originating in the Ming Dynasty and flourishing during the Qing, this vibrant folk tradition has regained its brilliance in modern times and earned international acclaim. The dance consists of two main branches: the dragon lantern dance—featuring forms like the Grand Wriggling Dragon, the Fire Dragon, and the Straw Dragon—and the festive lantern dance, which includes acts such as “Carp Leaps Over the Dragon Gate,” “Mudfish Eating Dumplings,” and “Three Dragons.” Steeped in cultural symbolism, the Tongliang Dragon Dance expresses values of unity, vitality, and harmony with nature. While a few iconic forms like the Fire Dragon remain widely recognized, many others are on the verge of extinction and in urgent need of preservation. In this episode, the host travels to Chongqing to meet with four inheritors of the Tongliang Dragon Dance. Through their stories, we uncover the rich legacy of this dazzling tradition, explore the deep roots of dragon culture in the region, and trace the origins of one of China’s most awe-inspiring folk arts.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber seeks out Liu Weixin, a master of Pak Mei kungfu and on whom the hit game "Sifu" was based. He experiences for himself this style's relentless and lightning-fast strikes, but also learns from its master how to balance life and kungfu, how a master should treat his disciples, and what it means to "eat porridge at night"

programme.title: Foodwise: Fuding
programme.desc: The hosts are in Fuding, Fujian Province in southeast China for the Dragon Boat Festival, where teams of rowers compete against each other in narrow dragon-shaped boats. From making and eating zongzi rice dumplings to trying local street food, the hosts take part in the festivities before exploring the world of white tea, from visiting its “mother tree” to drinking it in a zen temple, and even feasting on a white tea banquet!

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuyi Mountains
programme.desc: The hosts are in the Wuyi Mountains of Fujian Province, the birthplace of oolong tea. Here they enjoy tea ceremony on a bamboo raft, feast on everything from smoked goose to lotus seed soup, and explore an ancient town that once sold tea to Russia. They discover that here it’s all about terroir, and that nestled within the cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains is the most expensive tea in the world.

programme.title: Grand Song of the Dong — Natural Oriental Harmony
programme.desc: The Grand Song of the Dong is a polyphonic folk singing tradition of the Dong ethnic group. Performers from several villages gather together to sing, unaccompanied. The songs, which describe the history, beliefs, customs, and emotions of the Dong people, are an important part of their cultural identity and contribute significantly to their social cohesion. Generally sung in the Dong language, which has no written form, they are passed on orally from one generation to the next. Classified into various genres—including narrative and love songs, drinking and funeral songs—they are often accompanied by clapping, stomping, and dancing. Sung on occasions such as festivals, weddings, and funerals, the Grand Song, as a valuable part of the Dong ethnic group’s cultural heritage, reflects their wisdom and creativity, as well as their harmony with nature.

programme.title: Time travel in Shunde: From ancient ancestral halls to dim sum
programme.desc: Two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia embarked on a journey to the historic Yang'e Village in Shunde, Guangdong Province. There, they savored authentic morning tea, visited ancient ancestral halls to appreciate the architectural grace and clan heritage of Lingnan, and experienced intangible cultural heritage to the rhythm of lion dance drums.

programme.title: Outkirts of Wenzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He explores Wenzhou’s counties. From geological wonders and daring cliffside stunts at the Yandang Mountains, to rafting along the scenic Nanxi River, to harvesting seaweed and shellfish on the mud flats of the Dongtou Islands, Tianran discovers the ingenious ways the people of Wenzhou have transformed the challenges of living between mountains and seas into their greatest strengths.

programme.title: Life in Camel Town
programme.desc: When it comes to Mongolian, most people will think of grasslands, horse racing. In fact, the camel is the king of five livestock of nomadic people. Camel is the meritorious?figure in the vast desert on the Silk Road. In this episode, we go to Alashan: Camel Town in China, to experience the life of Mongolian people and camels in desert. Milking, delivering milk and collecting camels, also has a thrilling journey to pick up the newborn baby camel. We deeply feel the profound feeling between the camel raiser and their camels.

programme.title: Inner Mongolia’s Frozen Wonderland
programme.desc: In this episode, we feature the Winter Nadam Fair and winter sports in Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia. By late December, the Hulunbuir Grassland is blanketed in ice and snow. Even in the bitter cold of around 30 degrees below zero, the grassland is alive with a festive bustle.

programme.title: Dream Builders: Stories from China and Europe
programme.desc: On the occasion of the 50th anniversary of diplomatic relations between China and the EU, Inheritors of China launches a special multimedia series titled “Dream Builders: Stories from China and Europe.” Taking culture as the starting point, the series responds to public discourse by telling the real-life stories of Europeans living in China. Through their perspectives, it vividly illustrates how tradition and modernity spark mutual inspiration between China and Europe—showcasing a relationship of shared growth, empowerment, and enduring partnership. The series travels through cities including Beijing, Shanghai, Jinan, and Datong, focusing on Europeans of different ages and professions—from programming and installation art to music, calligraphy, and martial arts. Their lived experiences offer fresh insight into how cultural exchange between China and Europe continues to gain vitality, and how mutual learning between civilizations breathes lasting life into practical cooperation.

programme.title: Ding Porcelain Firing
programme.desc:
In ancient times, skilled craftsmen combined clay with fire and, using nothing more than their hands and wisdom, created the history of porcelain.
A thousand years ago, at the time of the Northern Song Dynasty, a type of porcelain was produced that stood out for its exquisite quality, elegant coloring and beautiful patterns. This was Ding porcelain, and it became a favorite at the imperial court. However, within 200 years, amid the chaos of constant warfare, the art of making it was lost. The dazzling white light of the Ding kilns had faded, seemingly forever.
And yet, 800 years later, that light has been reignited.

programme.title: Exploring the Long Winter
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Jingpo Lake, Xuexiang and Yabuli in Mudanjiang, showcasing the unique winter ice fishing festival, the fairytale-like scenery of Xuexiang, and its world-class ski resorts.

Through their perspectives, it vividly illustrates how tradition and modernity spark mutual inspiration between China and Europe—showcasing a relationship of shared growth, empowerment, and enduring partnership. The series travels through cities including Beijing, Shanghai, Jinan, and Datong, focusing on Europeans of different ages and professions—from programming and installation art to music, calligraphy, and martial arts. Their lived experiences offer fresh insight into how cultural exchange between China and Europe continues to gain vitality, and how mutual learning between civilizations breathes lasting life into practical cooperation.

programme.title: Ding Porcelain Firing
programme.desc:
In ancient times, skilled craftsmen combined clay with fire and, using nothing more than their hands and wisdom, created the history of porcelain.
A thousand years ago, at the time of the Northern Song Dynasty, a type of porcelain was produced that stood out for its exquisite quality, elegant coloring and beautiful patterns. This was Ding porcelain, and it became a favorite at the imperial court. However, within 200 years, amid the chaos of constant warfare, the art of making it was lost. The dazzling white light of the Ding kilns had faded, seemingly forever.
And yet, 800 years later, that light has been reignited.

programme.title: Time travel in Shunde: From ancient ancestral halls to dim sum
programme.desc: Two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia embarked on a journey to the historic Yang'e Village in Shunde, Guangdong Province. There, they savored authentic morning tea, visited ancient ancestral halls to appreciate the architectural grace and clan heritage of Lingnan, and experienced intangible cultural heritage to the rhythm of lion dance drums.

programme.title: Exploring the Long Winter
programme.desc: In this episode, we travel to Jingpo Lake, Xuexiang and Yabuli in Mudanjiang, showcasing the unique winter ice fishing festival, the fairytale-like scenery of Xuexiang, and its world-class ski resorts.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Pak Mei
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber seeks out Liu Weixin, a master of Pak Mei kungfu and on whom the hit game "Sifu" was based. He experiences for himself this style's relentless and lightning-fast strikes, but also learns from its master how to balance life and kungfu, how a master should treat his disciples, and what it means to "eat porridge at night"

programme.title: Foodwise: Fuding
programme.desc: The hosts are in Fuding, Fujian Province in southeast China for the Dragon Boat Festival, where teams of rowers compete against each other in narrow dragon-shaped boats. From making and eating zongzi rice dumplings to trying local street food, the hosts take part in the festivities before exploring the world of white tea, from visiting its “mother tree” to drinking it in a zen temple, and even feasting on a white tea banquet!

programme.title: Foodwise: Wuyi Mountains
programme.desc: The hosts are in the Wuyi Mountains of Fujian Province, the birthplace of oolong tea. Here they enjoy tea ceremony on a bamboo raft, feast on everything from smoked goose to lotus seed soup, and explore an ancient town that once sold tea to Russia. They discover that here it’s all about terroir, and that nestled within the cliffs of the Wuyi Mountains is the most expensive tea in the world.

programme.title: Grand Song of the Dong — Natural Oriental Harmony
programme.desc: The Grand Song of the Dong is a polyphonic folk singing tradition of the Dong ethnic group. Performers from several villages gather together to sing, unaccompanied. The songs, which describe the history, beliefs, customs, and emotions of the Dong people, are an important part of their cultural identity and contribute significantly to their social cohesion. Generally sung in the Dong language, which has no written form, they are passed on orally from one generation to the next. Classified into various genres—including narrative and love songs, drinking and funeral songs—they are often accompanied by clapping, stomping, and dancing. Sung on occasions such as festivals, weddings, and funerals, the Grand Song, as a valuable part of the Dong ethnic group’s cultural heritage, reflects their wisdom and creativity, as well as their harmony with nature.

programme.title: Time travel in Shunde: From ancient ancestral halls to dim sum
programme.desc: Two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia embarked on a journey to the historic Yang'e Village in Shunde, Guangdong Province. There, they savored authentic morning tea, visited ancient ancestral halls to appreciate the architectural grace and clan heritage of Lingnan, and experienced intangible cultural heritage to the rhythm of lion dance drums.

programme.title: Outkirts of Wenzhou
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran He explores Wenzhou’s counties. From geological wonders and daring cliffside stunts at the Yandang Mountains, to rafting along the scenic Nanxi River, to harvesting seaweed and shellfish on the mud flats of the Dongtou Islands, Tianran discovers the ingenious ways the people of Wenzhou have transformed the challenges of living between mountains and seas into their greatest strengths.

programme.title: Life in Camel Town
programme.desc: When it comes to Mongolian, most people will think of grasslands, horse racing. In fact, the camel is the king of five livestock of nomadic people. Camel is the meritorious?figure in the vast desert on the Silk Road. In this episode, we go to Alashan: Camel Town in China, to experience the life of Mongolian people and camels in desert. Milking, delivering milk and collecting camels, also has a thrilling journey to pick up the newborn baby camel. We deeply feel the profound feeling between the camel raiser and their camels.

programme.title: Inner Mongolia’s Frozen Wonderland
programme.desc: In this episode, we feature the Winter Nadam Fair and winter sports in Hulunbuir, Inner Mongolia. By late December, the Hulunbuir Grassland is blanketed in ice and snow. Even in the bitter cold of around 30 degrees below zero, the grassland is alive with a festive bustle.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. He learns from a Hung Ga master that while this kungfu style is often associated with brute force, it’s actually a combination of hard and soft techniques that can also be used in traditional Chinese massage. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.1
programme.desc: In this episode Tianran and Hannah are in Hangzhou, a city with over 2000 years of history and capital of two ancient Chinese dynasties. From the famous West Lake to delicate Dragon Well tea, our hosts experience Hangzhou's must-do attractions, savouring the local cuisine and trying everything from winter melon shaped like pork belly, to food cooked according to Traditional Chinese Medicine principles, and even Buddhist noodles and Zen tea.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran and Hannah continue their tea-tasting journey along Hangzhou's Qiantang River, exploring the region's historical culture and culinary delights. They head to Anding Mountain, enjoying misty tea at the summit. In Longmen Ancient Town, they dive into traditional Chinese clan culture and savor “Sun Quan seitan”. In the gentrified village of Shishe, Hannah falls in love with “gray soup rice dumplings”, while at Qiandao Lake Tianran tries the best fish head and beluga caviar he’s ever had in his life. Their journey ends with a cup of Jiukeng tea and a visit to ancient tea trees.

programme.title: Indigo Dreams: A Hue of Dali Tie-dye
programme.desc: Dali Tie-dye is the unique textile art of the Bai people, renowned for its exquisite hand-tying and traditional indigo dyeing techniques that create brilliant, one-of-a-kind patterns. Explore the cultural heritage and enduring beauty of this ancient craft from Yunnan.

programme.title: Village Voyage: Before the icon Bruce Lee, there was Shunde in Foshan
programme.desc: Nunchucks. Dark shades. A yellow jumpsuit. That unmistakable nose wipe. Blinding punches and the snake feint – one name says it all: Bruce Lee, the man who brought Chinese martial arts to the world. But every legend has a beginning – and his is less well known. It started in Shunde of Foshan City, south China's Guangdong Province. Join Julian Waghann from the US and Absalom Absalom from Namibia as they trace Lee's roots – following the footsteps of an icon back to where it all began.

programme.title: The Pulse
programme.desc: “The Pulse” features musicians performing amidst Guizhou’s stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: Bird-eye China Ep.1
programme.desc: Unfolding between the Kunlun, Altai and Tianshan ranges, cradling two vast basins, lies a beautiful land: Xinjiang. Join us on an aerial journey as we ascend the Tianshan to reveal the life-giving secrets of its crystal clear waters, before touching the summit of Bogda Peak, towering 5 km above sea-level, and gliding over the glittering, gem-like Tianchi Lake and the boundless grasslands that extend far beyond what even a bird’s eye can see into the west….

programme.title: Village Voyage: Before the icon Bruce Lee, there was Shunde in Foshan
programme.desc: Nunchucks. Dark shades. A yellow jumpsuit. That unmistakable nose wipe. It started in Shunde of Foshan City, south China's Guangdong Province. Join Julian Waghann from the US and Absalom Absalom from Namibia as they trace Lee's roots – following the footsteps of an icon back to where it all began.

programme.title: Three Gorges of Chongqing
programme.desc: In this episode, through the new fashion of five-star cruise tour on the Three Gorges, with comfortable and convenient high-end experiences, we take the audience to travel along the river, multi-dimensionally show the most spectacular and beautiful landscape gallery along the Yangtze River, feel the unique charm of canyons, rapids and cultural relics on both banks, and convey the new charm of Yangtze River cultural tourism.

programme.title: Valentine's with the Snake King
programme.desc: Every year on Qixi Festival (Chinese Valentine's Day), the town of Zhanghu in Nanping, Fujian Province hosts a folk custom event: the Snake King Parade. Local residents carry the statue of the Snake King from the temple, along with specially prepared pythons, and parade through the streets and alleys. Wherever the procession passes, residents and shopkeepers greet them with firecrackers and burn incense to pray, hoping to receive the unique blessing of the Snake King. This distinctive folk activity is rarely seen elsewhere across China. Taking this event as its highlight, the episode leads audiences on a deep dive into the towns and villages of northern Fujian, delivering a highly engaging and visually appealing viewing experience.

programme.title: Valentine’s for the Pumi People
programme.desc: In this episode, we record the grand celebration of the traditional Pumi Valentine's Day in Luoguqing, Lanping County, Yunnan Province. Every year, on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month, young men and women from the local community gather on the vast meadows of Luoguqing to take part in singing and dancing activities in pursuit of marriage. During the program, the host interacts with local people of the Pumi and other ethnic groups, showcasing the traditional plateau lifestyle of the Pumi people, their distinctive firepit culture, as well as the community’s brand-new look in the new era. All these scenes unfold against the lively backdrop of the Valentine’s Day activities, fostering a warm atmosphere of ethnic solidarity.

programme.desc: “The Pulse” features musicians performing amidst Guizhou’s stunning natural scenery, bringing to life a harmonious blend of music and landscape.

programme.title: Bird-eye China Ep.1
programme.desc: Unfolding between the Kunlun, Altai and Tianshan ranges, cradling two vast basins, lies a beautiful land: Xinjiang. Join us on an aerial journey as we ascend the Tianshan to reveal the life-giving secrets of its crystal clear waters, before touching the summit of Bogda Peak, towering 5 km above sea-level, and gliding over the glittering, gem-like Tianchi Lake and the boundless grasslands that extend far beyond what even a bird’s eye can see into the west….

programme.title: Village Voyage: Before the icon Bruce Lee, there was Shunde in Foshan
programme.desc: Nunchucks. Dark shades. A yellow jumpsuit. That unmistakable nose wipe. Blinding punches and the snake feint – one name says it all: Bruce Lee, the man who brought Chinese martial arts to the world. But every legend has a beginning – and his is less well known. It started in Shunde of Foshan City, south China's Guangdong Province. Join Julian Waghann from the US and Absalom Absalom from Namibia as they trace Lee's roots – following the footsteps of an icon back to where it all began.

programme.title: Three Gorges of Chongqing
programme.desc: In this episode, through the new fashion of five-star cruise tour on the Three Gorges, with comfortable and convenient high-end experiences, we take the audience to travel along the river, multi-dimensionally show the most spectacular and beautiful landscape gallery along the Yangtze River, feel the unique charm of canyons, rapids and cultural relics on both banks, and convey the new charm of Yangtze River cultural tourism.

programme.title: Valentine's with the Snake King
programme.desc: Every year on Qixi Festival (Chinese Valentine's Day), the town of Zhanghu in Nanping, Fujian Province hosts a folk custom event: the Snake King Parade. Local residents carry the statue of the Snake King from the temple, along with specially prepared pythons, and parade through the streets and alleys. Wherever the procession passes, residents and shopkeepers greet them with firecrackers and burn incense to pray, hoping to receive the unique blessing of the Snake King. This distinctive folk activity is rarely seen elsewhere across China. Taking this event as its highlight, the episode leads audiences on a deep dive into the towns and villages of northern Fujian, delivering a highly engaging and visually appealing viewing experience.

programme.title: Valentine’s for the Pumi People
programme.desc: In this episode, we record the grand celebration of the traditional Pumi Valentine's Day in Luoguqing, Lanping County, Yunnan Province. Every year, on the fifth day of the fifth lunar month, young men and women from the local community gather on the vast meadows of Luoguqing to take part in singing and dancing activities in pursuit of marriage. During the program, the host interacts with local people of the Pumi and other ethnic groups, showcasing the traditional plateau lifestyle of the Pumi people, their distinctive firepit culture, as well as the community’s brand-new look in the new era. All these scenes unfold against the lively backdrop of the Valentine’s Day activities, fostering a warm atmosphere of ethnic solidarity.

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Hung Ga and Choy Li Fut
programme.desc: In Foshan, China, Kleber meets with two masters of southern Chinese martial arts. He learns from a Hung Ga master that while this kungfu style is often associated with brute force, it’s actually a combination of hard and soft techniques that can also be used in traditional Chinese massage. Next, Kleber meets a master of Choy Li Fut, a kungfu style that utilizes everyday items such as towels, fans and even abacuses, and discovers the link between martial arts and lion dance.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.1
programme.desc: In this episode Tianran and Hannah are in Hangzhou, a city with over 2000 years of history and capital of two ancient Chinese dynasties. From the famous West Lake to delicate Dragon Well tea, our hosts experience Hangzhou's must-do attractions, savouring the local cuisine and trying everything from winter melon shaped like pork belly, to food cooked according to Traditional Chinese Medicine principles, and even Buddhist noodles and Zen tea.

programme.title: Foodwise: Hangzhou Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, Tianran and Hannah continue their tea-tasting journey along Hangzhou's Qiantang River, exploring the region's historical culture and culinary delights. They head to Anding Mountain, enjoying misty tea at the summit. In Longmen Ancient Town, they dive into traditional Chinese clan culture and savor “Sun Quan seitan”. In the gentrified village of Shishe, Hannah falls in love with “gray soup rice dumplings”, while at Qiandao Lake Tianran tries the best fish head and beluga caviar he’s ever had in his life. Their journey ends with a cup of Jiukeng tea and a visit to ancient tea trees.

programme.title: Indigo Dreams: A Hue of Dali Tie-dye

programme.title: Kungfu-wise: Taiji Quan
programme.desc: Kleber travels to Chenjiagou in central China, the birthplace of Chen-style Taiji Quan. Also known as tai chi, the martial art is iconic for its slow movements and purported health benefits, but Kleber quickly discovers it’s the real deal: From being thrown around by teenagers to learning about the martial art’s Yin-Yang philosophy, Kleber experiences for himself how this kungfu style allows small to defeat big, and soft to beat strong.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shantou
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in Shantou, Guangdong Province in south China, where they drink more tea than anywhere else in the country. They'll savor the complex aroma of the curiously named "Duck Poo Fragrance" tea, as well as enjoy a more traditional "yum cha" breakfast. They get a taste of traditional handicrafts, from breaking bowls to make inlaid porcelain to rolling "kueh" rice cakes, and feast on everything from sweet and savory street snacks to the finest seafood dining.

programme.title: Foodwise: Shaoguan
programme.desc: Tianran and Hannah are in the picturesque city of Shaoguan in Guangdong Province, South China. They try tea grown on Danxia landforms and feast on mountain produce, before getting hands-on with making rice noodles in a Hakka walled village. They learn about the Hakka people’s southward migration and the effect it had on local tea and food, and end their journey in a thousand-year-old Buddhist temple, seeing how the monks integrate their practice into everyday life, and discovering just why tea is so important to Zen.

programme.title: Forged in Legend: A Glimpse of Longquan Blades
programme.desc: Longquan swords, legendary blades from China, embody centuries of masterful craftsmanship. Forged with unique folding techniques and a distinctive star-patterned finish, these swords are renowned for their sharpness, resilience, and artistic value. Discover the rich history and cultural significance of these revered symbols of Chinese heritage.

programme.title: Shunde’s Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong—a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. Once, boats carried silk down its canals from small villages, building a legacy of trade. Today, Xiangyunsha (gambiered Canton gauze) is a global fashion icon, and historic spots like Mingshi Garden draw tourists and locals alike. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter—that’s the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.1
programme.desc: The Xiangjiang River runs 800 kilometers through the whole of Hunan Province. Hailed as the mother river of Hunan, it serves as a vital waterway connecting the Yangtze and Pearl River systems. Its source is located in Yongzhou, a land of abundant water resources, rich natural treasures and outstanding people. In this episode, we focus on three young women from Yongzhou: Pan Haiying, a dance teacher; Huang Cuilan, an inheritor of brocade weaving; and Hu Xin, a custodian of Nüshu culture. We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing
programme.desc: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing delves into the historical origins and cultural background of Fengdu Ghost City, and also features the Zhongyuan Festival celebrations and ancestor-worshipping rituals held here. These activities reflect the local people’s positive and optimistic outlook on life and death, as well as the great importance they attach to their ancestors, families and family traditions.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.2
programme.desc: Heilongjiang, China's northernmost province, is home to a veritable sea of trees, a forest forged by the Greater and Lesser Khingan Ranges. Beginning our Odyssey at its very northern extremity - a land of snowy Arctic snowscape and dazzling rime-frosts that's a paradise for winter-sports daredevils - we then head for Harbin and its spectacular ice festival in pursuit of some unique snowy adventures...

We document snippets of their daily lives and work, to reflect the profound cultural heritage along the Xiangjiang River and the value pursuits of the women living on its banks.

programme.title: Women of the Xiangjiang River Ep.2
programme.desc: In this episode, we continue our journey along the Xiangjiang River in Hunan Province, to meet more outstanding women from the cities of Hengyang and Zhuzhou. By documenting snippets of the daily lives and work of a paper-cutting artist, the director of the Hengyang Huagu Opera Troupe, and an inheritor of Liling porcelain craftsmanship, we gain vivid insights into the distinctive cultural traditions of this region.

programme.title: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing
programme.desc: Exploring the Folklore of Chongqing delves into the historical origins and cultural background of Fengdu Ghost City, and also features the Zhongyuan Festival celebrations and ancestor-worshipping rituals held here. These activities reflect the local people’s positive and optimistic outlook on life and death, as well as the great importance they attach to their ancestors, families and family traditions.

programme.title: Bird's-eye China Ep.2
programme.desc: Heilongjiang, China's northernmost province, is home to a veritable sea of trees, a forest forged by the Greater and Lesser Khingan Ranges. Beginning our Odyssey at its very northern extremity - a land of snowy Arctic snowscape and dazzling rime-frosts that's a paradise for winter-sports daredevils - we then head for Harbin and its spectacular ice festival in pursuit of some unique snowy adventures...

programme.title: Shunde’s Waterways: where business smarts meet everyday life
programme.desc: Shunde, a district in Guangdong Province, lies in the Pearl River Delta, north of Hong Kong—a water-rich region that lives by water and knows how to turn it into opportunity. Once, boats carried silk down its canals from small villages, building a legacy of trade. Today, Xiangyunsha (gambiered Canton gauze) is a global fashion icon, and historic spots like Mingshi Garden draw tourists and locals alike. With water as their muse and grit as their guide, Shunde folks keep business thriving while making life sweeter—that’s the quiet wisdom flowing through their rivers. Now, two friends, Julian Waghann from the United States and Absalom Absalom from Namibia are setting out to explore more with the locals...

programme.title: Escape to Yibin
programme.desc: Yibin is hailed as "The First City along the Yangtze River", home to renowned Yibin Ranmian noodles and Wuliangye liquor. We explored plenty of lesser-known scenic spots: Lizhuang, the cultural hub during the War of Resistance against Japanese Aggression; vast bamboo groves that embody the hermit culture of China; and the mysterious cliff-hanging coffins. It is precisely these secluded and strategically advantageous lands that enabled local cultures to be well preserved amid turbulent times.

programme.title: Korela Fortress Museum, Russia
programme.desc: 4K Documentary on Korela Fortress Museum, RussiaAt 160 km from St. Petersburg, there is a small town in northern Russia: Priozersk. Here, on the picturesque banks of the Vuoksa River's mouth and Lake Ladoga, stands the Korela Fortress Museum. Medieval Korela was the most northwestern city of Russia on the Vuoksa River island and served to protect against the Swedes' attack. The foundation date of the Korela Fortress is considered to be 1310. This Fortress is the only surviving Swedish bastion-type Fortress in Russia, on which unique buildings of 6-8 centuries are located: Lars Torstenson's Round Gate Tower, the Old Arsenal, the Powder Magazine, and the Suvorov Arsenal. Initially, the buildings of the Fortress were wooden, but numerous fires destroyed them. Over three centuries, the defensive structure was rebuilt and fortified many times. In the 15th century, Korela occupied an area of 6 thousand square meters, consisted of hundreds of log houses, and its population was more than 300 people. The people of the city were engaged in agriculture and fishing and also professed Christianity.By the sixteenth century, the Fortress acquired the form that has survived to this day. In the eighteenth century, the defense served as a prison for essential state criminals. The round gate tower of Lars Torstenson, located at the junction of the north-west and south-west curtains, is a Swedish building. The time of its construction dates back to 1583-1585. In plan, the tower has an almost circular shape, slightly elongated in the western and eastern directions. During its existence, the Fortress has changed more than one name. ""Korela"" repeatedly passed from Sweden to Russia and back and later belonged to Finland. Each country called this place differently. The original name ""Korela"" came from the name of a tribe that once lived in this area. It's interesting to know that until 19-century Korela was located on an island washed on both sides by the Vuoksa river. Due to its favorable geographic location, the Fortress was practically impregnable.

programme.title: Hook Down, Wheels Down
programme.desc: Produced in the early 1970s, "Hook Down, Wheels Down" was one of the most comprehensive (and expensive) films made by the U.S. Navy. It covers the history and development of the U.S. aircraft carrier, and does so through interviews with many of the men who made it happen. While dozens of aircraft carriers are featured, it is the USS John F. Kennedy (CV-67) that takes center stage -- and the material shot on her deck looks like it is right out of "Top Gun". There is wonderful flight op footage, great aerial flight footage, incredible WWII dog fightand bombing footage as well as endless aircraft carrier operational footage. Also shown in this film are very rare images of the first aircraft carrier USS Langley (CV-1) (formerly collier USS Jupiter AC-3). The follow on vessels are widely featured including USS Lexington (CV-3) and the USS Yorktown (CV-5) in the Battle of Coral Sea. Also featured: USS Saratoga (CV-2), USS Enterprise (CV-6), USS Hornet (CV-8), USS Wasp (CV-7), USS Ranger (CV-4), USS Yorktown (CV-5), USS Essex (CV-9), USS Guadalcanal (CVE-60), the British carrier HMS Furious, the destroyer USS Zeilin (DD-313), and many other warships. Various incidents are shown from Pearl Harbor, Midway, Coral Sea, the capture of the submarine U-505, the Marianas Turkey Shoot, the Doolittle Raid on Japan, and more. Includes interviews or appearances by many WWII naval aviators and aces including Wade McClusky, John Jay Courtney, Billy Mitchell, Gerald Bogen, Leslie Generes, John S. Thatch (of "Thatch Weave" fame), Ensign George Gay, David Campbell (whose Minsi III appears in the film), Edward "Butch" O'Hare, Charles Lindbergh, Glenn Curtiss, Clark Gable and Wallace Beery. Planes seen in the film include the Wright Brothers flier, biplanes, Lindbergh's Spirit of St. Louis, the NC-4 Flying Boat, Hellcat, Avenger, Corsair, Vindicator, Devastator, Wildcat, and Japanese Zero. Also seen in the film: dogfights, combat flying, the Washington Conference on battleships, the Panama Canal exercise of 1929, air mail service.

programme.title: US Carrier Fights for Life - USS Yorktown Battle of the Coral Sea World War II
programme.desc: This short newsreel, produced for the home market, shows the aircraft carrier USS Yorktown (CV-5) under attack by Japanese Zeros during the Battle of the Coral Sea. Although the carrier was badly damaged in the battle, it lived to sail another day and proved crucial to the U.S. victory at Midway a few months later.

programme.title: USS Langley
programme.desc: The “new navy” is the focus of this 1969 educational documentary presented by the United States Navy — “The Attack Carrier: From USS Langley CV1 to USS Enterprise CVAN65.” The color film traces the development and history of aircraft carriers used by the United States Navy. Aircraft that have been used by the Navy, such as the Grumman A-6 Intruder and McDonnell Douglas F-4 Phantom II, also are featured.

programme.title: USS New Jersey (BB-62)
programme.desc: Written by historian Richard Hough and presented by the U.S. Navy, the late-1960s film The American Dreadnought gives viewers a brief history of the American battleship USS New Jersey and a solid background of this class of ship. The film opens by taking viewers to the spring of 1921 where planes sink battleships as part of the agreement to cease battleship production following World War I. The film then cuts to 1966 and shows viewers retired battleships sitting idle at a remote pier in the Philadelphia Navy yard. The three ships are the Iowa, Wisconsin, and New Jersey.

programme.title: World War II Victory Ship Film
programme.desc: The Hannibal Victory was a new Victory ship, designed to transport critical supplies to the war effort faster than the older Liberty ships. This first part of the narrative focuses on its initial mission to transport a large shipment of U.S. Army cargo, including railroad car wheels, underframes, and eight locomotives, from San Francisco to a destination somewhere across the Pacific.

programme.title: WWII US Coast Guard film- Task Force
programme.desc: The film focuses around Coast Guard "Task Force" duty. Besides operational glimpses, the viewer is treated to a snapshot of the life of a Coast Guardsman on and off duty. While the film contains much documentary-style footage, some sections of the film are re-enactments and the scenario presented (in which the USCG battles a German U-boat and then lands troops on a Pacific Island) seems somewhat fanciful.

programme.title: America's Cup Race- Sailing Ships
programme.desc: This late 1930s or early 1940s film AWAY WITH THE WIND features various ships and water activities. It includes rare footage of clipper ships at the 10 second mark, and square riggers. Fishing on the Grand Banks is seen at the 1:00 mark. The Gertrude L. Thebaud is seen at the 1:08 mark. This is an American fishing and racing schooner built and launched in Essex, Massachusetts in 1930. A celebrated racing competitor of the Bluenose, it was designed by Frank Paine and built by Arthur D. Story for Louis A. Thebaud, and named for his wife, Gertrude Thebaud. In their first meeting at Gloucester, Massachusetts, in October 1930

programme.title: Ready on Arrival
programme.desc: The USS Independence CV-62 is the carrier featured. Carrier aircraft making attack runs over Vietnam are shown at the start of the film, landing on carrier decks at mark 1:00. At mark2:55, 4500 men are on the ship, they make it run; engineers, doctors, pilot, aircraft mechanics, fire men. They all help in running the ship. They work 14hours a day. They handle tons of explosives, works, and mechanics work all day keeping all the aircrafts ready when needed.

programme.title: Heritage of the Hornet
programme.desc: Heritage of the Hornet is a short 1970s film from McDonnell Douglas that looks at the heritage of the McDonnell Douglas F-18 Hornet—a heritage that is a history of naval ships, starting with the first Hornet in 1775 up through the eighth Hornet, which was decommissioned in 1970. The film opens with shots of the ocean, waves rolling in and hitting against rocks, and U.S. Navy ships at sea.

programme.title: The new Porsche 911 GT3 R - Design
programme.desc: The turbocharged three-litre flat-six in the new 911 GTS delivers 353 kW (480 PS). Maximum torque is 570 Nm, an increase of 20 Nm over its predecessor. Zero to 100 km/h takes just 3.3 seconds (911 Carrera 4 GTS: Fuel consumption combined (NEDC) 10.5 – 9.7 l/100 km, Fuel consumption combined (WLTP) 11.4 – 10.6 l/100 km, CO₂ emissions combined (NEDC) 240 – 222 g/km, CO₂ emissions combined (WLTP) 259 – 240 g/km) in the 911 Carrera 4 GTS Coupé with the eight-speed Porsche dual-clutch transmission (PDK): three tenths faster than its predecessor. A seven-speed manual transmission with a particularly short throw is available for all 911 GTS models as an alternative to the PDK.

programme.title: From concept vehicle to full-production ID. Buzz - How was the electric Microbus created
programme.desc: The new model line’s assistance systems perfect ease of driving and safety. Included as standard in the ID. Buzz and ID. Buzz Cargo is the ‘Car2X’ local warning system, which utilises signals from other vehicles and the transport infrastructure to spot hazards in real time. Also included as standard: the ‘Front Assist’ emergency braking function and, in the MPV, the ‘Lane Assist’ lane-keeping assistant. With new software, new assistance functions are also making their way into the ID. family. Available as an option is ‘Travel Assist with swarm data’, which facilitates partially automated driving across the entire speed range and, for the first time, assisted lane-changing on the motorway. Also new: the ‘Memory Function’ for automated parking on a previously saved route.

programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

programme.title: Colour change with the power of thought - The BMW iX Flow meets neuro-technology
programme.desc:
The Munich-based startup brainboost used the new and improved colour-changing effect in a one-off collaboration with the BMW Group at rad°hub aimed at raising awareness of mental health.
With the help of brainboost, the BMW iX Flow was connected directly to the brain of the rad°hub delegates using an electroencephalograph (EEG), which records the brain’s electrical activity. “The colour patterns of the BMW iX Flow react to brain activity and reflect the level of activity,” explains brainboost CEO Philipp Heiler. “Once the brain is at rest, the changes of patterns on the iX Flow also become calmer and more rhythmical.” A special animation was activated if delegates managed to maintain this state for several seconds. Thus, the participants were able to gradually calm and relax their brains under the guidance of the brainboost experts and with the help of neurofeedback via the iX Flow. This matures the knowledge of which strategies work best to specifically shut down one's own brain activity for relaxation, e.g. in everyday working life.

programme.title:
To celebrate the arrival of the new Bentayga EWB, an exclusive First Edition is now available. Subject to a limited production run for the first twelve months of orders, it combines many of the most desirable options available for the car with a package of eye-catching details found only on Bentley First Editions.
First Edition badging can be seen to the exterior of the car – a theme that extends inside, with badging on the veneered fascia, as well as embroidery on the seats. Unique First Edition contrast stitching and embroidery adorns the seats and, depending on the choice of veneers, handcrafted metal overlays just 0.075 mm thick can be applied to the fascia and waistrails in the front and the rear door veneer.
The First Edition offers elegant and timeless design, focusing on maximum comfort and well-being. This specifically tailored specification includes a unique 22” ten-spoke directional wheel and bright lower bumper grilles. Other additional features as standard include unique quilted seats, mood lighting, a heated steering wheel, and increased driver’s assistance aids. Attention to detail is clear, from the badging that identifies the car to the jewelled caps on the fuel and oil fillers.

programme.desc: The new model line’s assistance systems perfect ease of driving and safety. Included as standard in the ID. Buzz and ID. Buzz Cargo is the ‘Car2X’ local warning system, which utilises signals from other vehicles and the transport infrastructure to spot hazards in real time. programme.title: New 2023 Range Rover Sport Design Reveal Film
programme.desc:
The New Range Rover Sport has made its global premiere with a dramatic world-first climb up a flooded dam spillway in Iceland.
The epic ascent saw New Range Rover Sport resist the surging torrent of water flowing down the ramp of the Karahnjukar Dam – the biggest of its kind in the world – at a rate of 750 tonnes per minute. A loss of traction risked plunging down the perilous 90m drop at the base of the spillway to the valley floor below.
The successful spillway ascent was screened for the first time at an exclusive launch event at Jaguar Land Rover’s Advanced Product Creation Centre at Gaydon, UK.
Official James Bond stunt driver Jessica Hawkins was behind the wheel as the New Range Rover Sport demonstrated its grip, traction, performance and composure, completing the latest in a series of challenges for Land Rover’s luxury performance SUV. Previous feats include a record-setting hill-climb at Pikes Peak, a first recorded crossing of the ‘Empty Quarter’ desert in the Arabian Peninsula and a first ascent of the 999 steps to Heaven’s Gate in China, in 2018.

programme.title: Hispano Suiza showcases its history in the Peralada Castle Museum
programme.desc:
The history of Hispano Suiza is showcased, for the very first time, in the Peralada Castle Museum (Girona, Spain) where visitors will be able to contemplate the past and present of the legendary car brand founded in 1904 by Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt.
The Hispano Suiza Room will close the usual tour of the Peralada Castle Museum. After years of researching to gather the largest number of pieces and objects related to its history, Hispano Suiza becomes part of this important collection. The Hispano Suiza exhibition encompasses a journey through various decades: from the beginning of the 20th century, when Hispano Suiza was founded, to the present day. After passing through a luxurious hall, the public will be able to visit a recreation of the offices of Damián Mateu and Mark Birkigt, where countless business and technical ideas, emerged and took shape, turning Hispano Suiza into a point of reference, for luxury, comfort and technical solutions. In this area, the original painting 'Dame with a mink' by Ramon Casas takes pride of place: it was used as an illustration on the company's original shares.

programme.title: TechDay Digital Light - Digital Future Lighting
programme.desc: Safety and customer satisfaction come first at Audi. They are part and parcel of the success of the company with the four rings. In that context, light technology is steadily growing more important and creating a wider range of possibilities and perspectives, from added safety for the driver, to external communication and individualization. Systematic light digitization is making all of this possible. It is particularly visible in the new Audi A8: the forward-looking Digital Matrix LED headlights and digital OLED rear lights raise the customer experience to a whole new level: for the first time in any Audi model, light is completely digitized. The car can be individualized even further through its digital OLED rear lights. The Digital Matrix LED headlights also include three new functions: advanced traffic information, a lane light with direction indicator lights on highways, and an orientation light on country roads. These features not only demonstrate Audi’s “Vorsprung durch Technik,” they also add value.

programme.title: Mercedes-Benz DRIVE PILOT Sensors S-Class
programme.desc: The exact location of a Mercedes equipped with DRIVE PILOT is determined using a high-precision positioning system that is much more powerful than conventional GPS systems. In addition to the anonymised data collected by LiDAR, camera, radar and ultrasound sensors, a digital HD map provides a three-dimensional image of the road and the surroundings with information on road geometry, route characteristics, traffic signs and special traffic events (e.g. accidents or road works). This high-precision map differs from maps for navigation devices by, among other things, its higher accuracy in the centimetre rather than metre range and its detailed junction and route model. The map data is stored in backend data centres and updated constantly. Each vehicle also stores an image of this map information on board, constantly compares it with the backend data and updates the local dataset as required. All of this enables stable and accurate positioning through a representation of the surroundings that is independent of factors such as shadows or dirty sensors.

programme.title: Kia Sportage Exterior Design in Lunar Silver
programme.desc:
A number of new technologies optimize the precision and control of the chassis in a wide variety of weather and road conditions. The standard electronic damper control (Electronic Control Suspension, ECS) in the GT-line version increases comfort and safety thanks to the continuous damping control. The system reacts to body movements and steering inputs and changes the damping behavior at lightning speed in order to counteract the vehicle's diving, pitching and rolling movements when cornering. It also adjusts the damping force in the case of obstacles in order to cope with them as comfortably as possible and to reduce the influence of post-vibrations on the wheels.
A premiere for the Sportage is the “All-Terrain-Mode”, which will be available for the plug-in hybrid version with all-wheel drive. The system offers intelligent support when driving off-road or on snow by automatically optimizing the vehicle settings depending on the selected mode and thus helping the SUV to achieve maximum traction on muddy, sandy or snowy surfaces.

programme.title: The new Mercedes-Benz GLC AMG Line World Premiere Teaser
programme.desc:
The new GLC is immediately recognisable as a member of the Mercedes-Benz SUV family. Standard equipment includes the AVANTGARDE exterior with Chrome package including chrome window surrounds and a new, chrome-look simulated underguard. This adds striking design features and enhances the unique proportions of the vehicle. One of the defining design highlights of the GLC is the redesigned front end, with headlamps that connect directly to the radiator grille to emphasise the vehicle’s width, and the new radiator grille as part of the standard AVANTGARDE exterior, which now has a chrome surround and a sporty louvre in matt grey with chrome trim. The AMG Line has a radiator grille with Mercedes-Benz pattern.
The body design is characterised by a full, spanned surface design enriched with precisely shaped edges in the sides. These emphasise the proportions, accentuate the muscular wheel arches and create a balance between elegance and off-road performance. Wheel arch liners in the vehicle colour are available from the AMG Line upwards for the first time. These accentuate the sportiness of the AMG Line, as optional equipment in conjunction with mixed tyres. Also available as an optional extra are easy-entry running boards and, from the AMG Line upwards, a Night package.
